Vt.bar_b_note: The elder villager's sculpt, readable warm face, big eyes and green/brown outfit sit at Palworld-class character finish; only the noisy shell-fur hair and beard and the flat grey studio light hold it back.

Eo.bar_b_note: The blue-grey translucent panel has the right base, but there is no teal interaction or gold progression accent, the hints are keyboard-first, and B's tiny truncated text reads as a debug menu, not a shipped UI.

Lf.bar_b_note: Same elder villager as Vt: appealing face, clear silhouette and a palette that fits the world reach shipping character finish; the fuzzy hair/beard shells and neutral light are the only weak points.

Kg.bar_b_note: A murky, low-value brown forest floor with no purple storm sky or lightning grade, flat magenta telegraph rings, a hard-to-find player creature and a HUD that covers much of the frame (plus B's camera inside foliage at i13/i15) sink it next to Palworld's bright, readable boss fights.

Bs.bar_b_note: The standing wolf is close to the owner's Tanglevolt bar, but A's faint frames float above a detached shadow and swap to black/white patches, and B's faint end tips nose-down and vertical, so neither side holds a shipping finish through the pose set.

Gc.bar_b_note: The craftsman's chunky silhouette, apron and green scarf are on-palette, but the low-res, flat-painted face with tiny slit eyes reads mobile-tier next to Palworld's characters.

top_changes.change: Kg Stormwood fight: add a collision-aware combat camera that pulls clear of trunks and canopy, lift exposure and rim-light both fighters against the dark floor, add the purple storm sky/lightning grade, and replace the flat magenta telegraph rings with ground-crack or lightning telegraphs; trim the HUD during fights

Eo crafting panel: keep side A's text scale but show the full scrollable recipe list without truncation, give recipe subtext higher contrast, use teal for the selected recipe and gold for craftable/progress, and make the Craft/Leave hints controller-first gamepad glyphs

Creature faint set (Bs): ground the faint mid/end animation so the body stays on its shadow and settles on its side, and keep the storm-fur material through the faint instead of swapping to black/white patches; also give the Gc craftsman a higher-res face texture with livelier eyes
